name: TCAN330GDCNR
title: 3.3 V CAN and CAN FD transceivers with silent, standby and shutdown options
summary: TCAN330, TCAN332, TCAN334 and TCAN337 are single-supply 3.3 V high-speed CAN transceivers for ISO 11898-2 buses, specified to 1 Mbps; the G versions (TCAN330GDCNR is the TCAN330G in SOT-23-8 on a 3000-piece reel) add loop-delay symmetry limits for CAN FD up to 5 Mbps. Pins 5 and 8 choose the extras: shutdown, silent, standby with bus wake, or an open-drain fault output. The bus pins survive ±14 V, work over ±12 V common mode and carry ±12 kV IEC contact ESD protection; TXD and RXD dominant time-outs, undervoltage lockout, thermal shutdown and current limiting protect the bus, and an unpowered part does not load it.

circuits.title: Typical 3.3 V application
circuits.description: A 3.3 V node. The input supply passes a series diode into a 3 V voltage regulator, with a capacitor at its input and one at its output. The regulated rail feeds the microcontroller, with its own capacitor, and the transceiver's VCC, which has a capacitor to ground at the pin. The microcontroller drives TXD and pin 5 and pin 8 and reads RXD. CANH and CANL leave for the bus; at a node that ends the bus, an optional split termination of two resistors with a capacitor from their centre to ground goes across them.

parts.note: pin 5 is SHDN, NC or FAULT and pin 8 S, NC or STB, by device

notes: C4 is the 100 nF ceramic VCC decoupling capacitor; R1 and R2 are each half of a 120 Ω termination. R1, R2 and C5 sit only at a node that ends the bus.
On a TCAN337 the MCU line on pin 5 reads FAULT; on a TCAN334 the line on pin 8 is STB; on a TCAN332 both pins are NC.

circuits.title: Layout example parts
circuits.description: The parts of the board layout example around U1. TXD and RXD each pass a series resistor, and a capacitor from the TXD pin to ground filters it. Two capacitors, a bypass and a bulk, sit across VCC and GND at the pins. CANH and CANL go through a split termination (R5, R6 with C6 from their centre to ground), then each carries a capacitor to ground and a TVS diode before the two-pin bus connector. Pin 8 has a series resistor and a filter capacitor to ground; pin 5 has the same, and on the pin side of its series resistor a FAULT line with a pull-up resistor to VCC for the TCAN337 FAULT output.

parts.note: pin 5 SHDN or FAULT, pin 8 S or STB, by device

parts.value: TVS diode, CANH and CANL to ground

notes: The pin 5 and pin 8 parts (R3, R4, C4, C8, R7) depend on the device: R7 only on the TCAN337, whose pin 5 is FAULT.
A pull-up of 1 kΩ to 10 kΩ on TXD is needed when the host drives TXD from an open-drain output.

circuits.title: FAULT output to a microcontroller
circuits.description: TCAN337 only. The open-drain FAULT pin has a resistor up to VCC and goes to a fault input of the microcontroller. The output transistor turns off, letting the line rise high, on a TXD or RXD dominant time-out, thermal shutdown or undervoltage lockout.
notes: U1's other pins are not part of this circuit.

circuits.title: Typical CAN bus
circuits.description: Four nodes on one two-wire bus, each an MCU or DSP with a CAN controller and a CAN transceiver. A termination resistor goes across CANH and CANL at each end of the bus, one on the cable at the first node and one inside the last node.

parts.value: MCU or DSP with CAN controller (node 1)

notes: RTERM is typically 120 Ω, equal to the cable's characteristic impedance.
The other nodes' controller links and every node's supply pins are not part of this circuit.

circuits.title: Standard termination
circuits.description: A single resistor across CANH and CANL at a node that ends the bus, matching the cable's 120 Ω characteristic impedance.
notes: U1's other pins are not part of this circuit.

circuits.title: Split termination
circuits.description: The termination as two 60 Ω halves in series across CANH and CANL, with CSPLIT from the centre to ground. It filters the bus common mode and keeps it steady as messages start and end, which lowers emissions.
notes: U1's other pins are not part of this circuit.

circuits.title: Supply current test circuit
circuits.description: TXD is driven and the bus is loaded with RL and CL in parallel from CANH to CANL; the supply current is measured.
notes: U1's other pins are not part of this circuit.

circuits.title: Driver test circuit
circuits.description: A signal into TXD; RL and CL in parallel across CANH and CANL, with VOD read across them and VO(CANH), VO(CANL) read to ground. Delays run from the 50% points of TXD to VOD crossing 0.9 V and 0.5 V; rise and fall times between 10% and 90% of VOD.
notes: U1's VCC and RXD are not part of this circuit; S, STB and SHDN are held at 0 V.

circuits.title: Receiver test circuit
circuits.description: A differential input VID between CANH and CANL (CANL at 1.5 V, CANH stepped to 3.5 V); RXD drives CL_RXD to ground. Delays run from VID crossing 0.9 V and 0.5 V to the 50% points of RXD; rise and fall times between 10% and 90%.
notes: U1's other pins are not part of this circuit.

circuits.title: Mode change time test circuit
circuits.description: TXD held at 0 V while a step on SHDN, S or STB changes mode; RL and CL load the bus and RXD drives CL_RXD. tMODE runs from the control pin's 50% point to RXD's 50% point, or to VOD crossing 500 mV (into silent) or 900 mV (out of silent).
notes: The step is applied to SHDN, S or STB, whichever mode is under test.
U1's VCC is not part of this circuit.

circuits.title: Loop delay test circuit
circuits.description: A signal into TXD; RL and CL load the bus and RXD drives CL_RXD. tPROP(LOOP1) runs from TXD's falling 50% point to RXD's falling 50% point, tPROP(LOOP2) between the rising ones.
notes: U1's VCC, pin 5 and pin 8 are not part of this circuit; S, STB and SHDN are at 0 V.

circuits.title: Loop delay symmetry test circuit
circuits.description: RL and CL load the bus and RXD drives CL_RXD. TXD carries five dominant bits followed by one recessive bit of width tBIT. tBUS_SYM is the recessive width of VOD between its 500 mV and 900 mV crossings; tREC_SYM is the recessive width at RXD between 30% and 70%.

parts.value: bit pattern, tBIT = 500 ns or 200 ns

notes: U1's VCC, pin 5 and pin 8 are not part of this circuit.

circuits.title: TXD dominant time-out test circuit
circuits.description: TXD held low; RL and CL across the bus. tTXD_DTO runs from VOD rising through 0.9 V to it falling through 0.5 V while TXD stays low.
notes: U1's other pins are not part of this circuit.

circuits.title: Driver short-circuit current test
circuits.description: A switch connects CANH or CANL to a source VBUS stepped from 0 V; IOS is read 200 µs after the step.
notes: U1's other pins are not part of this circuit.

circuits.title: RXD dominant time-out test circuit
circuits.description: A differential input VID held dominant between CANH and CANL; RXD drives CL_RXD. tRXD_DTO runs between RXD's 50% points, from falling after VID passes 0.9 V to rising again while VID stays dominant.
notes: U1's other pins are not part of this circuit.

circuits.title: FAULT output test
circuits.description: TCAN337. A source between FAULT and GND sets the pin voltage while IFAULT is measured.
notes: U1's other pins are not part of this circuit.

operation.text: Eight 3.3 V CAN transceivers for ISO 11898-2 high-speed CAN, in SOIC-8 and SOT-23-8. TCAN330, TCAN332, TCAN334 and TCAN337 are specified to 1 Mbps; the G versions add loop-delay symmetry limits and run to 5 Mbps for CAN FD. The devices differ in pins 5 and 8: TCAN330 has shutdown and silent, TCAN332 normal mode only, TCAN334 shutdown and standby with bus wake, TCAN337 a fault output and silent.

Recessive (logic high, the idle state): the receivers' input resistors bias both lines to about 1.85 V common mode, with roughly 0 V between them. Dominant (logic low): one or more drivers force current through the terminations and a differential voltage appears; dominant overrides recessive, and several drivers dominant at once in arbitration give more differential voltage than one. In standby and shutdown the lines are instead weakly pulled to ground through the receiver input resistors.
Driver and receiver both work: TXD becomes the differential bus signal and the bus comes back on RXD.
S high turns the driver off and leaves the receiver running, so the node only listens; RXD follows the bus.

STB high turns off the driver and main receiver; a low-power receiver and bus monitor stay on and the bus lines are weakly pulled to ground. The host watches RXD for a high-to-low edge and returns the part to normal mode.

In standby the part looks for the ISO 11898-5 multiple filtered dominant wake-up pattern (WUP): a filtered dominant, a filtered recessive, then a second filtered dominant; other traffic in between does not reset the monitor. Once the pattern is seen, every dominant longer than tWK_FILTER drives RXD low. A bus state shorter than tWK_FILTER(MIN) never counts, one longer than tWK_FILTER(MAX) always counts, and one between may count. The pattern and filter time keep noise and a stuck-dominant bus from raising false wakes. Going to normal mode or an undervoltage on VCC clears the wake request.
SHDN high gives the lowest current: driver and receiver off, RXD high, bus lines pulled to ground. No wake from the bus is possible in this mode.

Active in normal mode, where the driver works. A falling edge on TXD starts a timer; if TXD has not risen within tTXD_DTO the driver turns off and the bus is free for other nodes. A high on TXD clears it. During the time-out RXD still follows the bus and the bus pins stay biased recessive.

In every device a bus held dominant longer than tRXD_DTO releases RXD high, so a stuck bus cannot hold the controller's input low. RXD follows the bus again once the bus goes recessive; the bus pins are biased recessive meanwhile.

Above the shutdown temperature the driver turns off, blocking TXD to the bus, while the bus pins stay biased recessive and the receiver path to RXD keeps working. It recovers when the junction cools below the threshold, with hysteresis to keep the driver from oscillating; a persisting fault makes it cycle, and long operation like that can reduce reliability.

When VCC falls below the undervoltage threshold the part enters protected mode: the bus goes high-impedance with its common mode biased to ground, RXD goes high-impedance, and no bus signals pass. Unpowered, the bus pins and logic pins leak very little, so the node does not load a running bus or the circuits still powered around it. Power-up and power-down are glitch-free on the bus.

The open-drain FAULT pin is held low in normal operation and turns off on a TXD dominant time-out, an RXD dominant time-out, thermal shutdown or undervoltage lockout; with an external pull-up to VCC the line then goes high.

TXD has a weak internal pull-up and S, STB and SHDN weak pull-downs, so open pins settle in normal mode with the driver recessive. These are a fallback, not something to design on, especially with noise. With an open-drain TXD driver the weak pull-up is not enough for CAN bit timing: an external pull-up of 1 kΩ to 10 kΩ is needed.

Driver current is limited in both dominant and recessive states, and the TXD time-out keeps the higher dominant short-circuit current from lasting. Bit stuffing, control fields and interframe space guarantee some recessive time even with mostly dominant data, so the average current follows the recessive-to-dominant ratio. Size termination and other network parts for the short-circuit and fault cases; a supply shorted across a termination resistor usually drives far more current through it than the transceiver limit.

The bus pins withstand ±25 kV HBM and ±12 kV IEC 61000-4-2 contact discharge on chip. The IEC model's 150 pF and 330 Ω (against 100 pF and 1.5 kΩ for HBM) give much larger discharge currents; air-gap levels are inferred from contact results.
All devices run from one 3.3 V nominal supply, with TTL input and output thresholds, and connect directly to 3.3 V controllers.

The dominant differential output is between 1.5 V and 3 V into 60 Ω, the same limits 5 V transceivers meet, and the terminations, not the driver, set the recessive state. The receiver gives recessive below 500 mV and dominant above 900 mV over –2 V to 7 V common mode, as a 5 V receiver must. The recessive bias is set above half of VCC to match the dominant common mode, which improves EMC; noise on VCC moves this bias.

ISO 11898 gives up to 1 Mbps, 40 m of cable, 0.3 m stubs and 30 nodes; careful design can exceed these, and standards such as CANopen allow up to 1 km with changes to termination, cable, node count and rate. The driver meets 1.5 V into 50 Ω over –12 V to 12 V common mode through a 330 Ω coupling network, a load equal to 120 TCAN33x receivers at their 40 kΩ minimum differential input resistance; margin for cable loss, imbalance and ground offset lowers the practical count.

The cable is twisted pair of 120 Ω characteristic impedance, terminated at both ends with resistors equal to it; stubs are kept short. If termination lives in a node, that node must not be removable from the bus. Split termination, two 60 Ω halves with a capacitor from centre to ground, steadies the common mode at the start and end of messages and lowers emissions.
Decouple VCC with a 100 nF ceramic capacitor as close to the pin as possible. The TPS76333 linear regulator suits the 3.3 V supply.

Start the layout with the protection and filtering: ESD and EFT energy spans about 3 MHz to 3 GHz. Place TVS diodes and bus capacitors at the connector, in the signal path, so transients do not reach other nets. Put bypass and bulk capacitors right at the supply pins, and use at least two vias for the VCC and ground connections of bypass and protection parts. Series resistors can limit current in the logic lines, and small capacitors at the input side can filter them. The TCAN337 FAULT pin needs an external pull-up.
